note: Requirements extracted from Eric's skills, rules and repo configs, with sources. IDs are stable references for the specs.

workflows.name: ship-quality-code (team lifecycle map)
workflows.summary: Master map of Eric's team workflow from intake to production with roles (Eric, Orchestrator, PM, Engineering, Auditor, Librarian, Hypothesizer, Jev, coding agents) and approval rules. Adds Jev chore triage with a light loop, a CRL-count table by change type, PR hygiene, merge/spend/post approval rules, audit-engagement and D2 false-positive gates, and checklists. Section 12 lists seven unresolved open decisions.

workflows.name: implementation-workflow
stages: Opus-class plan: smallest change, goals, non-goals, done-looks-like
Load coding rules at full intensity
Lazy first draft (Cursor Cloud Agent if available), watch CI
Exit -> Review step 1 (CRL); Solidity also Auditor
workflows.summary: Standard path for confirmed product asks: plan with the strongest model, build the narrowest draft, split by stack, freeze, and hand off to review. Every feature must pass the code-review loop at least once; Solidity src/ changes also run the Auditor workflow, and larger Solidity features run the loop twice. Stack-specific skills are placeholders to be filled later.

workflows.name: code-review-loop (Claude copy, current)
stages: A2 Open questions to user (parallel with Step 1)
B Step 1: 4 parallel read-only tracks (Minimize, Rules, Bugs, Anti-slop) with Evidence rule in each
E Step 2 on NEW diff with swapped model family: Late Minimize + Late Rules
workflows.summary: Mandatory multi-track review for all feature work with context-free read-only reviewers, Jev (TypeSafe) gating, and a separate Patch agent. Step 2 re-reviews the post-patch diff on a different model family. Includes Test scope rules that keep full suites in CI and STE/anti-slop/evm-cortex companions.

workflows.name: code-review-loop (Cursor copy, older variant)
stages: Step 1: 5 parallel tracks (Minimize, Rules, Bugs, Anti-slop, Evidence)
workflows.summary: Earlier version in ~/.cursor: a separate Evidence reviewer track (five tracks), no A2 open-questions step, no Test scope section, and checks run full `forge test`. Its jev-gate.md adds an auth fallback to ~/.config/eng-secrets/TYPESAFE_API_KEY.

workflows.name: CRL light loop (chore path)
workflows.summary: Fast path for chore-level diffs outside Solidity src/. No Jev scoring of findings, no Step 2, no model swap; escalate to full if the diff grows into src/ or behavior.

workflows.name: auditor-workflow
stages: Phase 1 Orient (xray-pre-audit, audit-prep; mini-recon for PR-delta)
workflows.summary: Security engagement path for Solidity/Foundry, additive to the CRL. Agent-driven with optional human tag-in, isolated read-only depth workers, one shared thread list, a PoC bar by severity, and the same Jev policy as the CRL.

workflows.name: Audit engagement flow (Librarian/Hypothesizer)
stages: Engineering maps code, harness, fuzz suites
Hypothesizer proposes leads (hunt order: baselines, diff vs last audit, per-module, cross-module, fuzz gaps)
Auditor scores leads with Jev dedupe
Engineering PoCs confirmed TPs with control test
Submission after approval; revalidate before close
workflows.summary: External/competitive audit process with distinct Librarian, Hypothesizer, Auditor and Engineering roles. Requires a known-issues index before scoring, the D2 gate for Medium+, a fixed finding writeup format, and Eric approval before any filing.

workflows.name: evm-cortex New Protocol Feature
workflows.summary: Third-party (ccashwell) evm-cortex orchestrator routing that Eric loads as the Solidity cortex. Test-first sequence with a single code-reviewer agent and a verifier quality gate before deployment.

workflows.name: evm-cortex Bug Fix
workflows.summary: Reproduce-first bug fix path in evm-cortex. A PoC reproduces the bug before the fix, then the verifier gate runs.

workflows.name: evm-cortex audit pipeline (Light/Core/Thorough)
workflows.summary: evm-cortex audit-orchestrator modes by agent count (~15/~25/~40) and nSLOC/TVL. Eric's auditor-workflow reuses these phases but renames Light to PR-delta.

workflows.name: Foundry-first development cycle
workflows.summary: Rule loaded into every session (identical in ~/uniswap/evm-cortex/rules). Ends with a Before-Every-PR checklist: build, all tests, snapshot --check, slither, coverage.

workflows.name: Pre/post-deployment gate (test-before-deploy + protocol-qa)
stages: Post-deploy: code, verify, owner/roles, proxy impl, events
workflows.summary: Checklist gate before and after any Solidity deployment. Combined with ship-quality-code steps 10-14 (dry run, Eric go, broadcast, live verify, records).

workflows.name: protocol-planner
workflows.summary: Solidity planning agent template producing scope, dependency graph, implementation order, test matrix, deployment sequence, risk register and timeline.

workflows.name: planner / plan-reviewer agents
workflows.summary: Generic plan-only agents in ~/.claude/agents; ~/personal/agents/20260116-daily-automation-system.md is an output of this format. No code, explicit exclusions, API signatures, success criteria.

workflows.name: grilling (grill-me / grill-with-docs)
stages: Ask one question at a time with a recommended answer
Explore codebase instead of asking when possible
workflows.summary: Pre-build stress test of a plan through relentless one-at-a-time questioning. grill-with-docs also produces ADRs and a glossary.

workflows.name: handoff
workflows.summary: Compacts a session into a handoff doc for a fresh agent.

workflows.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
stages: Present findings; ask issue tracker, triage labels, domain docs one at a time
workflows.summary: One-time per-repo scaffold for issue tracker, triage label vocabulary (needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix) and CONTEXT.md/ADR layout.

workflows.name: auto-spec command (autonomous spec workflow)
workflows.summary: Generic command that runs spec-driven development fully autonomously and explicitly never asks the user for review. It conflicts with Eric's approval and intake rules.

workflows.name: Agentation watch mode (frontend feedback loop)
workflows.summary: Browser-annotation driven UI fix loop for the prospectus Next.js app.

requirements.statement: Record the ask verbatim as `original_ask` at intake; reviewers and Auditor receive it verbatim.
If the ask is ambiguous, stop and ask Eric (send back to Intake) before planning or coding.
Builds/bugs route Eric -> Orchestrator -> PM (spec) -> Engineering (build + CRL) -> Auditor (Solidity); Eric prefers builds go through PM, not directly to Engineering.
Small hotfix asks (for example a one-line README change): PM may start Engineering without a new confirmation from Eric.
Only Eric can waive the CRL: nits he marks "no code review loop" go in a separate small PR with no CRL.
Send product calls (UX choices, rule changes, spend) to Eric as one clear question with a recommendation.
Security questions or external findings route to the audit roles, not the build path.
For larger changes PM writes a concise spec covering edge cases, all product surfaces, and out of scope; the report identifies PM decisions Eric can overrule.
When Eric says "start with a spec", send the spec to Eric for review before any build.
Think from first principles: check what already exists (for example a v4-periphery entrypoint) before building a standalone contract; do first-principles spec re-reviews before build when asked.
Implementation starts only from a confirmed ask (Intake approved).
Plan only with the strongest available (Opus-class) writer model; never draft the plan with a weaker model.
Before any code, produce four plan components (in parallel): smallest change, goals, non-goals, done-looks-like (concrete acceptance checks: tests, UI, API behavior, CI green).
Never widen scope past non-goals; remove scope that is not necessary (for example support for already-deployed contracts).
When two designs solve the same problem, prefer the more explicit design; do not over-engineer against bad actors who can bypass the system anyway.
No conditional or nondeterministic logic in the hot path of a swap for fees; calculate at deploy time and cache.

Planner agent writes the plan to `{YYYYMMDD}-{plan-name}.md` (kebab-case, <=50 chars) with Scope (Included/Excluded), API signatures, steps, files, challenges, testing strategy, success criteria; no copy-pastable code; no extras (no backwards compat, legacy fallbacks, future-proofing unless requested).

Solidity protocol plans: interfaces before implementations, leaf contracts and libraries before consumers, tests planned with each contract, deployment sequence with verification gates and a rollback plan, audit readiness as a milestone.
Jev triage `is_chore` before implementation: noul >= 0.6 means light loop, else full loop; write `TRIAGE is_chore=<x> | path=light|full reason=...` in the gate log and the PR description.
Solidity `src/` in a Solidity repo skips triage and always gets the full loop; Solidity tests, TypeScript, React may use the light path.
Re-check triage at freeze; escalate to full if the diff touches `src/` or changes behavior.
Apply the project custom coding rules at full intensity (no relaxed mode); load the stack skill for the repo at Plan, Build and Split.

Lazy first draft: implement the narrowest change that meets done-looks-like; gather repo context first; launch a Cursor Cloud Agent with the plan and stack skill when available, else draft with the same constraints.
Give the coding agent the problem, constraints and done criteria; do not prescribe line edits.
Use the existing patterns of the repo ("Just need a script that follows the existing pattern in the repo"); no bespoke paths or one-wave scripts.
Stay quiet until there is a PR (or PRs) or a real blocker; do not surface noise to the user.
Engineering watches CI and comes back only with a PR or a blocker.
Full-stack changes: frontend and backend get separate PRs and pipelines per repo, each with its stack skill.
One coding agent per task; send follow-ups to the same agent (keeps branch and context); never start a second agent on the same task.
If a coding agent cannot create or update a PR, report the refusal; do not open the PR another way.
The orchestrator does not root-cause code itself; a coding agent investigates. Coding agents do all non-trivial repo work.
Foundry is the default for all Solidity testing, deployment and analysis, not Hardhat/Truffle.
Foundry TDD cycle: write interface/spec, write tests first (RED), implement (GREEN), `forge snapshot`, optimize, `slither .`, `forge coverage`, deploy via `forge script`.
Fixed pragma pinned to the tested compiler version; never `^0.8.x`.
Named imports only, grouped libraries -> types -> interfaces -> contracts; never wildcard imports.

Naming: contracts/libraries/types PascalCase, interfaces `I` prefix, functions/params/locals/modifiers camelCase, internal/private state and functions `_` prefix, constants UPPER_SNAKE or PascalCase, immutables camelCase, events PascalCase, errors PascalCase descriptive.

File layout SPDX -> fixed pragma -> imports -> contract; contract order: using, constants, immutables, state (mappings then scalars), events, errors, modifiers, constructor, external, public, internal, private, view/pure helpers.
Custom errors only (`selector.revertWith()` or `revert Err()`), with relevant parameters; never `require` with strings; single-line `if (...) revert` guards without braces.
Long function signatures: params on first line, then visibility, modifiers, returns on following lines.
Always use named mapping parameters and named-field struct construction (never positional).
`unchecked` only where overflow is provably impossible, always with a comment saying why.
Comments explain why, never what; code should be self-documenting.
Full NatSpec lives on the interface; implementations use `@inheritdoc`.
Every public/external function must have NatSpec (`@notice`, `@param`, `@return`); the natspec-enforcer hook flags missing NatSpec on public/external non-override functions.
Contracts carry `@title`, `@author`, `@notice`; `@custom:security-contact` is mandatory on all deployable contracts; units (decimals, bps, seconds) stated in `@param`/`@return`; no redundant docs.
Every contract MUST implement its corresponding interface containing all externally callable functions, errors and events (twap-auction repo rule).
Emit events for every state change; config changes include old and new values; index up to 3 filtered params; no indexed strings/bytes.
Emit events before external calls (hooks/callbacks) so events stay in chronological order.
Prefer custom types over raw primitives; use SafeCast for all narrowing conversions.
Constants are `private constant` with explicit type, placed after `using`; no inline literals except 0 and 1; underscores in large literals.
Forbidden: `tx.origin` auth, `selfdestruct`, `require` strings, floating pragma, wildcard imports, `abi.encodePacked` with dynamic types, inline assembly without documented safety justification.
Checks-Effects-Interactions always; ReentrancyGuard on functions with external calls (value/token paths at minimum); SafeERC20 for ALL token transfers; `Ownable2Step` over `Ownable`.

Validate all inputs at function boundaries (zero-address, bounds, array lengths); check low-level call returns; never trust external return data; never delegatecall untrusted targets; limit returndata copy.
Every state-changing function has explicit access control; timelock on admin functions affecting user funds; multisig for protocol-critical ops; document all privileged roles.
Never hardcode `1e18` for token amounts; query `decimals()` at initialization and store immutable; use explicit scaling; test with 6, 8 and 18 decimal tokens.
Never hallucinate contract addresses; verify with `cast code`/`cast call` before use; prefer factory/registry derivation; document each hardcoded address with its source.
Use native Circle-issued USDC only, never bridged variants (USDbC, USDC.e).

Gas: measure, do not guess (`forge snapshot`); calldata over memory, storage packing, immutables, cached SLOADs; do not optimize admin/rare paths; assembly only if savings exceed 20% on a hot path; never trade security for gas.

After each `.sol` edit, hooks run `forge build`, Slither (report High/Medium), `forge snapshot --check --tolerance 5` (warn >5% regression), NatSpec check, and storage-layout check for upgradeable contracts.
`forge fmt` clean and `forge build` with zero warnings (`--deny-warnings`).

foundry.toml defaults: pinned `solc_version`, `auto_detect_solc=false`, `ffi=false`, `extra_output=["storageLayout"]`, fmt (`line_length=100`, `int_types="long"`, `sort_imports=true`, `number_underscore="thousands"`), CI profile fuzz 10000 runs / invariant 1000 runs depth 100.

Upgradeable contracts: never remove/reorder/retype storage; append only and shrink `__gap`; `_disableInitializers()` in implementation constructor; `reinitializer(N)` for V2+; access-controlled `_authorizeUpgrade`; diff `forge inspect ... storage-layout`; test upgrade on fork; no selfdestruct.
Error design: `Module_ErrorName` prefixes, errors grouped by domain in interfaces, `@dev` on every custom error.
Write code as if audited tomorrow: document invariants as comments AND as invariant tests.
Say "onchain"/"offchain" (one word, no hyphen) in all writing.
Percentages in contracts use basis points (uint16, max 10000); Solidity time units; `ether` keyword for ETH amounts; checksummed addresses (EIP-55), never truncated in code.
No secrets in code: no private keys, API keys or RPC URLs in scripts; `.env` never committed; load with `vm.env*`; separate deployer keys for testnet and mainnet.
Secrets never appear in prompts, files, logs, chat or commits; name env vars only (for example `MAINNET_RPC_URL`); never print RPC URLs or keys.
Eric gives keys (API keys, deployer key) outside chat; keep them on the machine that uses them.
Fork tests skip cleanly when the RPC env var is not set.
Credential-deny hook blocks tool access to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, ~/.gnupg, .npmrc, .env*, credentials.json, private keys, terraform state, and bare env/printenv.

Test scope: run only tests the diff touches plus tests importing changed sources; never the full suite locally when CI runs it; if no CI runs it, run once at the end in background with the CI profile (`FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci`); reviewers and Patch agents never run the full suite.

Only one agent runs the test tool at a time; do not stash, checkout or switch branches during a test run; check pre-existing failures by running only the failed test at the base commit in a separate worktree.
Solidity checks: `forge build`, `forge fmt --check <changed files>`, `forge test --match-path <touched test files>`.
Non-Solidity stacks: project typecheck, lint, and unit tests for the changed files.
Never weaken tests or bars to make checks pass.
twap-auction local validation uses bounded runs, for example `forge test --fuzz-runs 64 --no-match-contract AuctionInvariantTest`, unless the user asks for a full suite.
Foundry test names `test_{action}_{scenario}`, fuzz `testFuzz_{action}`, contract `{Contract}Test`; vague names (`test_stuff`, `test1`) are anti-slop findings.
Invariant functions use the `invariant_` prefix; handlers bound inputs and do not revert; run depth 64+ and runs 256+.
Test edge cases explicitly: 0, 1, max, empty state, first deposit/last withdrawal, same-block interactions.

Test structure: Arrange/Act/Assert; `makeAddr()` + `vm.label()` (no raw addresses); `bound()` over `vm.assume()`; one assertion concept per test; minimal `setUp`; `vm.expectEmit` for events; fork tests pinned to a block number.
Coverage target: 90%+ line coverage on `src/`, 100% on security-critical paths.
All functions, lines and branches tested to 100% coverage in twap-auction; fuzz parameters where possible; dedicated edge/corner-case and invariant tests; differential tests for assembly.
New features merge with associated tests; bug fixes include a test that fails without the fix.
Fuzz: 256 runs local, 1000+ in CI, fixed seed; preserve counterexamples as regression tests.
Gas snapshots with forge-gas-snapshot require `forge test --isolate`; commit `.gas-snapshot` and fail CI past a threshold.
No useless tests: no assert-true or no-revert tests without meaningful state, no noise-only snapshot/golden tests, no duplicate coverage, no over-mocked tests that skip the real path.
Test layout: `test/unit`, `test/integration`, `test/fork`, `test/invariant`; abstract base fixtures; mocks in `test/mocks/`, helpers in `test/helpers/`.
ALL feature work, any stack, runs the Code Review Loop at least once before done; human PR review does not replace it.
Context-free reviewers: never review in the session that wrote the code; spawn separate subagents/chats; refuse author self-review. The author checklist is not a review.
Review tracks are read-only and emit findings only; only the Patch agent edits.
CRL required inputs: `original_ask` (verbatim), frozen `diff` or `changed_paths`, `language_stack`, `repo_root`; stop if any is missing.
Freeze ask, goals, non-goals, done-looks-like and a diff snapshot (commit SHA or saved diff) before review; the author stops editing until Patch; do not mutate the ask after freeze.
Record the frozen package, PR links, CI status and blockers in the notebook / PR description / notes file; keep it short.
Step 1 spawns four parallel context-free read-only tracks: Minimize, Rules, Bugs, Anti-slop; each gets only required inputs, companions and its track brief; wait for all before Jev.

Every finding uses schema `id, track, location, title, trigger, impact, severity, evidence, recommendation`; each needs a concrete trigger, impact and a `file:line` quote read in the file, else drop it.

Open questions run in parallel with Step 1: ask the user all design questions only they can decide in ONE message with a recommendation each, plus missing tools/credentials (for example `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, Step 2 CLI); ask finding-driven questions in one message before the gate; user-decision findings go to the user, not Patch.
Minimize reviewer cuts fat: dead code, unused exports, unreachable branches, over-abstraction, single-call-site helpers, features beyond the ask.

Rules reviewer applies in order: repo rules (AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING, style configs), STE CLAUDE.md, STE dictionary, then evm-cortex for `.sol`; prefers delete/inline, boring names, straight-line control flow.
Bugs reviewer: behavior vs ask and neighboring tests, edge cases, error paths, concurrency/reentrancy; for `.sol` use the cortex severity matrix (Impact x Likelihood).

For `.sol`/Foundry, Bugs and Rules load cortex rules (solidity-style-guide, security-first, severity-matrix, finding-output-format) and skills solidity-security, solidity-patterns, natspec-standards BEFORE judging; prefer `~/uniswap/evm-cortex/`.

Anti-slop (code): fail dead code, unused imports/locals, commented-out blocks, single-use wrappers/factories, cute names, pass-through layers, defensive code that cannot fail, duplicated logic or premature DRY.
Anti-slop (comments): fail AI residue ("Certainly!", "Let's"), narrating comments, filler `@notice` that repeats the name, TODO/FIXME/HACK without owner or ticket, changelog comments.
Anti-slop (docs/PR): fail verbose unrelated README sections, marketing fluff, emoji padding, decorative rules, prose that restates the diff.
Prefer delete over rewrite when text adds no information; any anti-slop hit that would merge is a finding.

Jev Gate: send ALL findings to Jev (`POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`, model `jev-latest`, `Authorization: Bearer $TYPESAFE_API_KEY`), batching questions; write one gate-log line per finding; pass only `ACTION=keep` rows to Patch.

CRL keep bar: `keep_drop=keep` AND `is_critical` noul >= 0.75 (optional High: severity >= 2.5, is_critical >= 0.6, confidence >= 0.5); `same_as_existing` >= 0.7 is a duplicate (keep stronger evidence); thresholds tuned in code, not prompts.

Jev is a noise/dedupe filter, NOT a severity filter: Bugs/Auditor keep if impact noul >= 0.6; Minimize/Rules/Anti-slop keep if mean of applicable `abstraction_worth_it`, `readability_gain`, `language_clear`, `test_required` >= 0.6; severity recorded for order only; coding agents get every kept finding of any severity.
Missing `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` stops the loop before Triage or Gate; never invent keep/drop; report the review as blocked, not passed.
Patch agent is a separate agent: receives only the kept set + gate log, dedupes overlapping patches, applies each kept item or rejects it with a reason, logs `APPLIED` / `REJECTED reason=...`.

Step 2 is mandatory, on the NEW post-patch diff only: Late Minimize + Late Rules in parallel, same Jev policy, fresh Patch agent (new session), Bugs once more only if code changed, checks, intent reviewer, ready PR, CI/review-bot findings through Jev, PASS.

Step 2 reviewers and Patch use a different model family than Step 1; log `step1_model_family`/`step2_model_family`; never claim a swap that did not occur; if a model fails, say the run was single-model.

Allowed models for review and build: Fable, Opus 5.5, Sol; each loop of a double loop uses a different one; parallel tracks use different models for variance (for example Bugs Fable, Rules Sol, Minimize + Anti-slop Opus 5.5); record model per step in the gate log.
Intent reviewer (fresh, read-only) confirms the final diff still satisfies `original_ask`.
Light loop (chore): freeze; ONE context-free reviewer+fixer applies only anti-slop and STE fixes; no Jev scores, no Step 2, no model swap; checks green; ready PR with the triage line.
Any change under Solidity `src/` (including merge resolutions, small edits, docs-adjacent PRs) gets the full CRL at least once AND the Auditor workflow.
Larger Solidity feature sets (new strategy/module, multi-file parameterization, economic/tick math, new launch paths) run the full CRL twice with a model swap, then Auditor.
Every deploy or broadcast script change gets a CRL (Auditor usually a quick pass).
"Heavy" CRL = full, at least two rounds, multiple independent context-free reviewers with a model swap, anti-slop and vocab filters on code AND copy.
"Double code review loop with Jev" = two full loops on different allowed models, then the whole PR goes to Auditor and Engineering waits for the result.
Audit-fix PRs get at least two passes: one anti-slop, one by the Auditor.
When Eric says code is too verbose, send it through a CRL and re-check after.
Skip iOS/device loops; optional screenshot gallery only if UI screenshots already exist.
Keep review artifacts and commits recoverable; verify the head SHA again before review.
Auditor workflow is additive to the CRL, never a substitute; it may read the CRL gate log but does not re-run Minimize/Anti-slop.
Auditor handoff: `original_ask`, `repo_root`, scope, frozen diff/PR, docs paths, optional CRL gate log and seed threads; stop if `repo_root`/scope missing (no blind audits).

Auto-select mode and record it: PR-delta (localized, <~3-5 .sol files, no new value flow), Core (new module/strategy, cross-contract value movement, >=~500 nSLOC), Thorough (pre-deploy, full audit, high TVL, governance-critical, prior Med+); when unsure prefer Core.

Audit is fully agent-driven; tag a human only on triggers: unconfirmed Thorough scope, missing docs/trust assumptions, verified Critical in production, blocked secrets/tools after one self-serve attempt, ambiguous scope.
Depth/Pashov/PoC workers are context-free subagents and read-only; they write only artifacts (threads, PoC tests under `test/`, reports); never edit production `src/`.

One shared thread list per engagement (prefer `audit/threads.md`) with `id, source, title, location, status, owner, poc, notes`; status `open -> investigating -> poc -> verified|dropped|deferred`; dedupe by location + bug-class; never close without evidence or drop reason.

Static triage with Slither and Aderyn: High/Medium (and sharp Lows) become threads; informational only if it touches value transfer, auth or upgradeability; note N/A in the log if tools are unavailable.
PoC bar: Critical/High need a full Foundry PoC; Medium needs a PoC or quantified impact; unverifiable claims are dropped or downgraded, never shipped as Critical/High.
PoCs: Foundry tests, pinned fork block, `makeAddr()`, `deal()`, log impact with `console.log`, assert the exploit succeeds, comment each step, minimal path.
Only verified (or strong-PoC) threads go to Jev, under the same Jev policy as CRL; write a gate log; coding agents see only the kept set + log.
Kept fixes go to Engineering or a fresh context-free Patch session, never the author session that wrote the vulnerable code.
After fixes Auditor re-checks the new head; a PASS carries over only when the delta does not touch reviewed code and Auditor says so explicitly.
When Eric asks, Engineering waits for the Auditor result and does not continue past the gate.
Deliverables by mode: PR-delta = PR review comments + thread snapshot; Core = short report section + PR comments; Thorough = full report via audit-report-generation.

Medium+ false-positive gate (D2) before filing and at every revalidation: single-change control test, fix-effectiveness test, named loser with cited entitlement (read the guard as design), counter-evidence search, "what makes this wrong?" revalidation, report-repo access; record `control_test`, `fix_test`, `loser_entitlement`, `design_intent_checked`.

Engagement kickoff collects repo, branch, pinned commit, in/out scope, prior audits, KNOWN_ISSUES, last audited commit, submission target/template, severity scale, deadline; layout `<engagement>/{refs,librarian,hypothesizer,auditor,eng,filing,diagram}`; new isolated workspace per engagement.

Librarian builds the known-issues index BEFORE any lead is scored; Hypothesizer leads carry contract:line, premise, why it can break, closest known issue, the quoted designed behavior, and no implementation details.
Do not report unfixed known issues; a partial fix or the same root cause via a new path is valid.

Finding writeup: summary, `#### Technical Details` (commit-pinned links, PoC, forge command + output), `#### Impact` (severity here), `#### Recommendation`, empty `#### Developer Response`; severity in label and Impact only, never the title.

Submission: one finding per issue, target template, duplicate check first (comment instead of duplicating), file only after Eric approves, batch Info/Low to Eric; revalidate each filed finding at the pinned commit before closing.
Investigation reports keep "confirmed finding", "bounded negative", "blocked" and "not tested" separate; state coverage limits; correct earlier rankings when new evidence arrives.
Audit readiness: code frozen, 90%+ coverage, gas snapshot committed, NatSpec complete, `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, architecture diagram and threat model in `docs/`, Slither clean or findings accepted.
Resolve every addressed GitHub review thread (a code fix is not enough); report "N of N threads resolved, 0 open".
No excess output committed: scratch logs, broadcast dumps, run output, `out/`, `cache/`; fix `.gitignore` if needed.
Remove what the ask no longer needs, with its tests; no verbose code or comments.
Open/mark the PR ready (never draft) after PASS, unless the orchestrator or Eric says keep it draft.
Do not force-push a shared branch unless the plan says so; prefer a new commit or a merge over a rebase that needs a force-push.
Readiness report keeps "ready for human review" separate from "merge-ready"; never claim a review PASS that did not run.
CI must be green; re-running a flaky job needs no Eric; a fix needing more token scope (for example `.github/workflows`) goes to Eric; Eric may waive the CI wait on test-only PRs.

Eric owns merges: no merge without his go; standing permission only on `zhongeric/imd-token-verify`; check `mergeable` and check runs first; maintainer approval still required on Uniswap repos; never approve a PR the user authored.
Stacked work follows Eric's order exactly; change a PR base when Eric says; force-push of `main` waits for whoever has permission.

PM's Engineering handoff lists: verbatim ask + spec path, repo/base/rebase order, workflow (implementation-workflow + Jev triage, CRL count, Auditor y/n), allowed models, merge owner, spend limits, report target and content (PR link, head SHA, tests, CRL + Auditor verdicts).

PR-ready checklist: CRL PASS recorded (triage line, gate log, model per step), Auditor PASS at current head for Solidity `src/`, threads N of N, no logs/dumps/scratch/verbose comments, no leftover code, CI green with tests not weakened, ready unless told otherwise.
Commit format `<type>: <description>` with types feat, fix, refactor, docs, test, chore, perf, ci, audit; keep commits atomic.
Commit summaries in lowercase imperative mood, <= 100 characters; PRs via Graphite (`gt submit`) preferred with conventional-commit titles.
Put new private repos for Eric's own projects under `zhongeric`; confidential work is never pushed or committed to public repos.
Dry-run the full deploy/broadcast on a fork first; report tx count, gas, native-token cost vs deployer balance, and predicted addresses.
Re-check onchain state immediately before broadcast (for example "no pool is initialized yet"); add stop-guards to scripts (decimals mismatch, out-of-range start, wrong factory).
Estimate native-token cost before a broadcast; send funding asks to Eric once, in one table, stating the shortfall.

Mainnet and paid actions run ONLY on Eric's own direct go (a relayed go does not count); broadcast waits for clean CRL and Auditor on the exact script and params; any param/address/salt change after the go needs a new go; no paid jobs, API spend or retries without his go; a pre-approved job runs only inside its scope.
Broadcast with exactly the verified params; chunk large jobs with a progress file so a resumed run skips completed rows; use the deployer key Eric set up and never print it.

Hook factories deploy via OpenZeppelin `Create2` from the factory (not the 0x4e59 proxy) and initialize the pool atomically in the same call; re-mine salts when the factory address changes; recompute addresses and code hashes independently before broadcast.
Deploy scripts follow the repo pattern (for example `new X{salt: ...}` with `vm.broadcast()`); no raw `CREATE2_DEPLOYER.call`, no unnecessary env overrides, no duplicate data files.

Pre-deploy gate: `forge build --force` zero warnings, `forge test` all pass with no skipped critical tests, `forge snapshot --check`, Slither no High/Medium (all triaged), coverage, storage layout matches previous deployment, contract size < 24KB, `forge script` simulation without broadcast.

Live verification by Auditor or a separate agent: code present, bytecode/code-hash match, flags, events, counts; scope every PASS explicitly; check consumer-facing interfaces (for example registry getters) before telling a partner; verify onchain before reporting deploy status (dry run is not a broadcast).
Post-deploy: contracts verified on explorer, deployer holds no admin roles, ownership moved to multisig/timelock, no lingering approvals, addresses recorded in `deployments/`.
Write a record file (for example `LIVE-RECORD.md`) with addresses, tx hashes, counts and spend; send Eric the tx hashes after a broadcast.

Solidity CI: build + size check first, parallel unit/fuzz/invariant jobs, gas snapshot diff comment with 5-10% tolerance, Slither SARIF on every PR, `forge fmt --check`, testnet auto-deploy on main, mainnet via manual `workflow_dispatch` with environment protection, `forge verify-contract` in pipeline, preserve broadcast artifacts.

Write in Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100 Issue 9) for chat replies, docs, reports, design docs, code comments and NatSpec; NOT for commit messages, PR titles/descriptions, identifiers, test names or tool inputs; precise technical terms (reentrancy, slippage, mainnet) are allowed.
STE sentence limits: max 20 words per procedural sentence, max 25 per descriptive sentence, one instruction per sentence, max six sentences and one topic per paragraph.

STE mechanics: no semicolons, no Latin abbreviations (e.g., i.e., etc.), no contractions, no phrasal verbs, no would/could/should/might or perfect/progressive tenses, active voice, American spelling, noun clusters of at most three words.
Look up uncertain words with `grep -i -A4 "^word " ~/.claude/ste/asd-ste100-issue-9.txt` (UPPERCASE = approved); never paste the STE dictionary into prompts.
Safety text uses WARNING/CAUTION; put conditions before instructions; notes give information, not instructions.
"Vocab filter" means the STE rules + anti-slop checklist applied to code AND user-facing copy.

Only the orchestrator reports or summarizes to Eric; other agents send results to the orchestrator and stay silent when nothing is new; keep messages short with PR/source links; answer Eric's questions directly first, then detail.
Never post, file, comment, send, publish or create a gist without Eric's explicit approval; draft first; post word for word as approved, then report the URL; track approved drafts until posted.
External audit platforms (for example Cantina) are read-only; investigations stay local; Auditor posts reviews only on internal Engineering PRs and nothing on external targets.
Keep work moving: look for deadlocks and idle work lanes and work around them.
Handoff docs go to the OS temp directory (not the workspace), include a "suggested skills" section, reference existing artifacts by path/URL instead of duplicating, and redact secrets/PII.
Grilling: interview one question at a time, with a recommended answer for each; explore the codebase instead of asking when it can answer.
Before exploring, read `CONTEXT.md`/`CONTEXT-MAP.md` and relevant `docs/adr/`; use glossary terms; flag ADR contradictions explicitly; proceed silently if the files are absent.
Agent config: edit the existing `CLAUDE.md` (else `AGENTS.md`); never create one when the other exists; ask which to create if neither; update an existing `## Agent skills` block in place.
Docs live next to code (NatSpec in contract) and are updated with the code.
Audit report writing: reference exact lines, give an actionable recommendation for every finding, state unclear impact honestly, quantify impact.
UI copy is minimal: icons over labels, no labels or filler.
UI rewrites keep detail available but hidden behind progressive disclosure.

UI polish (checkable): never `transition: all`; `will-change` only on transform/opacity/filter, never `all`; press scale exactly 0.96 (never < 0.95); interactive hit areas >= 40x40px with no overlap; `tabular-nums` on dynamic numbers; `text-wrap: balance` on headings, `pretty` on body; image outline 1px `rgba(0,0,0,0.1)` light / `rgba(255,255,255,0.1)` dark; `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased` on root; `AnimatePresence initial={false}`.

UI polish (judgment): concentric radius (outer = inner + padding), optical alignment, layered shadows over borders, interruptible CSS transitions, split/staggered enters (~100ms), subtle exits; icon swaps animate scale 0.25->1, opacity 0->1, blur 4px->0 (spring duration 0.3, bounce 0 if motion is installed).
UI review output is markdown Before/After tables grouped by principle, listing every change, one diff per row, omitting empty tables.

dApp: simulate before write (`useSimulateContract` -> `useWriteContract`), wait for receipt, batch reads with `useReadContracts`, handle idle/pending/confirming/confirmed and all error classes, explorer link while pending, chain guard, allowance-aware approval flow, typed ABIs and `0x${string}` addresses, loading states.

Next.js apps: App Router only (never Pages Router), `src/` with `@/*` alias, Server Components by default (`"use client"` only when needed), Tailwind utilities (no inline styles or CSS modules), TypeScript strict.
For new Next.js versions, read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing code and heed deprecation notices.
Agentation "watch mode": loop `agentation_watch_annotations`; for each annotation acknowledge, fix, then resolve with a summary until told to stop.
Leave no TODOs, placeholders or missing pieces; write only code necessary for the task.

TypeScript (tree-exploration): strict mode, explicit types over inference, `bigint` for Solidity numeric values, interfaces PascalCase without `I` prefix and preferred over type aliases, 2-space indent, semicolons.

protocol-audit-hub (team repo, CLAUDE.md authored by hensha256): implement only the requested phase, keep diffs minimal, Zod-validate every external input and vendor response, preserve raw vendor JSON, run `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` after meaningful changes, summarize changed files / check results / known gaps per phase.
protocol-audit-hub DB migrations: additive/nullable migrations to prod before deploying code; deploy-then-migrate for destructive changes; confirm before applying a prod migration.

TypeSafe/Jev integrations: read live docs first, keep known rules/calculations/execution in code, ask one narrow judgment per question, evaluate thresholds on the user's data, keep API credentials server-side.
Stripe: use the latest API version unless told otherwise; read the relevant reference before writing integration code; review the Go Live Checklist before launch.

Karpathy guidelines (enabled plugin): surgical changes, do not improve adjacent code or formatting, match existing style, remove only orphans your change created, state assumptions, define verifiable success criteria per step.

evm-cortex routing: route Solidity tasks to the most specific agent; opus for architecture, audit orchestration, depth analysis, planning, code review, pre-deploy verification; sonnet for implementation, tests, gas, deploy scripts.
